- When sentiment is high (≥0.7), model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to capture bullish momentum.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4), model over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid bearish overreaction.
- Model consistently under-estimates late-period spikes (last 5–7 days of forecast); apply a 2–5% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.
- Model over-estimates early-period drops (first 3–5 days of forecast); reduce by 1–3% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment is strong.
- Overshoot after spikes: if true outcome spikes >5% above forecast, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–4% in next period if sentiment is cooling.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment rises sharply in last 3–5 days, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag effect.
